title: Typed plans for existing guarded atomic task operations
request: Continue to TP-03 only, following the standing instruction to run only relevant tests and test groups for changed behavior and areas it may affect.
plan: Read the master specification and inspect existing core task contracts, registry checks, source adapter, gateway and harness.
Write failing success, dependency and argument tests before implementing a metadata-only per-task planner.
Reuse the frozen plan contract and exact existing stage/export capabilities, with pure source, argument, permission and budget checks.
Add one optional bounded gateway role with exact deterministic fallback, zero-cell context and saved API thinking summaries.
Run affected task tests and purpose/privacy checks, compare authored DEV cases, fix independent review findings and record acceptance.

decisions.decision: Keep one existing atomic stage or export as one planned action.
decisions.why: The current adapter already owns physical operation mapping. Splitting the final stage or using run_all would duplicate engine effects or cross the leaf boundary.

decisions.decision: Reuse core TaskExecutionPlan v1 and the existing pure graph, readiness and plan validators without schema changes.
decisions.why: The contract already represents argument references, evidence, budgets and stop policies. Registry-specific argument validation belongs in the R&D host.

decisions.decision: Recompile the source adapter and validate static arguments through the real pure Registry.check.
decisions.why: Current source and capability identity must be checked before planning. Core semantic checks alone do not validate the complete registered JSON argument schema.

decisions.decision: Bind prompt and model output schema as a fingerprinted policy input and expose a pure resolve_action gate.
decisions.why: Plan provenance is excluded from semantic fingerprints. Policy changes must invalidate stored plans, and future dispatch must refresh permissions and resolved arguments.

decisions.decision: Return a no-op for a human gate or verification task without declaring completion.
decisions.why: A gate requires authentic owner evidence. Planning cannot manufacture that evidence or consume holdout permission.

decisions.decision: Give the optional model its own off-by-default task_planner role using the existing one-attempt gateway bounds.
decisions.why: The role plans one execution intent rather than decomposing business problems or task groups. It needs no new client, agent loop or execution context.

decisions.decision: Pin the new prompt to dedicated DEV evidence without changing global gate policy.
decisions.why: The owner prohibits unrelated broad evaluations. Existing global snapshots become explicitly stale for the new prompt; no old result is rewritten or broad pass claimed.

change: Add deterministic typed plans for five existing binary stages and report export, pure current-source/schema/budget revalidation, explicit blockers and gate no-ops, bounded optional model proposals, exact fallback, privacy/thinking capture tests and a scripted DEV validity comparison. No task execution or rollout is added.

findings.defect: Tuple comparison rejected a harmless reorder of source references despite an identical semantic graph fingerprint.
findings.scenario: Reverse a valid graph's source reference order. Core validation and its canonical fingerprint remain valid, but the first planner implementation returns a changed-source blocker.
findings.cause: The host compared tuple order while the existing core fingerprint treats source references and several atomic fields as sets.
findings.fix: Compare source references by canonical identity tuples and normalize set-like atomic source steps, inputs, outputs and acceptance checks before comparison.
findings.test: The benign-order regression reverses source and atomic set ordering and requires a ready deterministic plan with the same fingerprint. The reviewer independently repeated the probes.
findings.impact: Equivalent graphs read through a different serialization order would be needlessly blocked.

findings.defect: The initial authored host-state helper copied an approval receipt fingerprint from a different fixture.
findings.scenario: The five-stage positive test reached final with a gate receipt whose approval reference did not match the supplied source approval fingerprint.
findings.cause: The reused test advancement helper assumed its original fixture's fixed digest.
findings.fix: Bind the authored gate receipt to the actual supplied approval fingerprint in the TP-03 helper; preserve strict production approval validation.
findings.test: The complete authored stage chain now yields ready stage plans while unready or consumed holdout states remain blocked.
findings.impact: A mismatched synthetic receipt prevented the positive final/report cases from testing valid behavior.

measurements.name: Test-first planner boundary
measurements.gate: The new positive and negative planner tests must fail before the planner implementation exists.
measurements.result: The new test module failed to import because dclab_rnd.tasks.planner did not exist; initial success, readiness and missing-argument tests then passed after implementation.

measurements.name: Relevant regression and integration tests
measurements.gate: All selected task, contract, validation, adapter, purpose-enumeration and new zero-cell privacy tests pass with no live calls.
measurements.result: 119 tests passed across planner 28, execution-plan contract 10, task validation 40 and adapter 41. Six targeted harness-enumeration and privacy inventory/caller tests also passed. No skips.
limits: Only affected test groups ran; there is no full repository or PostgreSQL gate claim.
The unchanged global prompt and harness snapshots are stale for the new task-planner prompt; its dedicated DEV freshness test passes instead under the owner's explicit scope instruction.

measurements.name: Scripted DEV plan validity comparison
measurements.gate: Every predeclared DEV outcome matches; invalid proposals retain the exact deterministic plan; no tool call, extra holdout access or live model call occurs.
measurements.result: All 24 authored scenarios passed. There were 15 scripted provider calls, nine exact invalid/unavailable fallbacks, zero tool calls, zero extra holdout accesses and zero live cost.
limits: One binary source fixture with simulated approvals and observations; no real execution evidence.
Scripted replies measure validator behavior, not live model quality, task completion or production readiness.

measurements.name: Independent adversarial review
measurements.gate: Every confirmed correctness finding is fixed and the current implementation has no remaining correctness finding.
measurements.result: Final review passed after the canonical-order fix. The reviewer independently verified equivalent reference, source-step, input, output and acceptance-check reorderings.

outcome: TP-03 complete under the owner's focused-test policy. Typed task plans, pure gates, optional bounded proposals, DEV evidence and independent review pass. TP-04 is not started.
lessons: A fingerprint's canonical set semantics must also be used by host freshness comparisons.
Plan readiness does not grant execution permission or prove completion; the existing runtime remains authoritative.
Keep a separate focused prompt attestation when broad evaluation snapshots are intentionally not refreshed; report the limitation explicitly.
Run affected tests once and expand only for concrete changes or review findings.
risks: Host-supplied approvals and verification receipts must be authenticated by the later runtime; pure JSON planning cannot authenticate them.
Only the existing basic binary adapter is supported. Complex programmes and other families remain blocked.
The future dispatcher must refresh actual bytes, permissions, locks, budgets and holdout receipts at the guarded effect boundary.
Synchronous model proposals need the existing POSIX main-thread deadline; unsupported callers retain deterministic fallback.
